questions.title: Express.js MCQ Quiz – 75 Multiple Choice Questions with Answers
questions.seo_description: Prepare for Express.js interviews with 75 MCQs covering middleware, routing, REST APIs, error handling, authentication, template engines, file uploads, and production best practices.
questions.intro: Express.js is the most popular, minimal web framework for Node.js, providing a flexible foundation for building web applications and REST APIs. These 75 MCQs cover Express fundamentals including routing, middleware, request/response objects, error handling, security, file handling, and REST API design patterns.

questions.question: What is Express.js?
options: A minimal, unopinionated web application framework for Node.js
questions.answer: A minimal, unopinionated web application framework for Node.js
questions.explanation: Express.js provides a thin layer of fundamental web application features on top of Node.js's HTTP module.

questions.question: How do you create an Express application?
questions.answer: const app = express()
questions.explanation: After `const express = require('express')`, you call `express()` to create the application object.

questions.question: What is middleware in Express.js?
options: A server between client and database
A function with (req, res, next) that executes during the request-response cycle
questions.answer: A function with (req, res, next) that executes during the request-response cycle
questions.explanation: Middleware can modify req/res objects, execute code, end the cycle, or call `next()` to pass control forward.

questions.question: What does `next()` do in Express middleware?
options: Goes to the next route file
Passes control to the next middleware function in the stack
questions.answer: Passes control to the next middleware function in the stack
questions.explanation: Calling `next()` hands off control to the next matching middleware or route. Without it, the request hangs indefinitely.

questions.question: What does `app.use()` do in Express?
options: Mounts middleware or a router on the app or a specific path prefix
questions.answer: Mounts middleware or a router on the app or a specific path prefix
questions.explanation: `app.use(middleware)` applies globally. `app.use('/api', router)` mounts a router at the `/api` prefix.

questions.question: What is `req.params` in Express?
options: An object containing route segment values captured from the URL, e.g., /users/:id → req.params.id
questions.answer: An object containing route segment values captured from the URL, e.g., /users/:id → req.params.id
questions.explanation: Route parameters (`:id`) are extracted from the URL path and available as `req.params.id`.

questions.question: What is `req.query` in Express?
options: An object containing URL query string key-value pairs, e.g., ?page=2&limit=10
questions.answer: An object containing URL query string key-value pairs, e.g., ?page=2&limit=10
questions.explanation: `req.query` automatically parses the URL query string: `?page=2` → `{ page: '2' }`.

questions.question: What is `req.body` in Express?
options: The parsed body of a POST/PUT/PATCH request, populated by body-parsing middleware
questions.answer: The parsed body of a POST/PUT/PATCH request, populated by body-parsing middleware
questions.explanation: `req.body` is `undefined` by default. Use `express.json()` or `express.urlencoded()` to parse it.

questions.question: What does `express.json()` middleware do?
options: Parses incoming requests with JSON payloads and populates req.body
questions.answer: Parses incoming requests with JSON payloads and populates req.body
questions.explanation: `express.json()` is built-in middleware (since Express 4.16) that parses `application/json` request bodies.

questions.question: What does `express.static(dir)` do?
options: Serves static files (HTML, CSS, JS, images) from the specified directory
questions.answer: Serves static files (HTML, CSS, JS, images) from the specified directory
questions.explanation: `app.use(express.static('public'))` serves files from the `public` folder directly without custom route handlers.

questions.question: What does `app.listen(port, callback)` do?
options: Starts the HTTP server and binds it to the specified port
questions.answer: Starts the HTTP server and binds it to the specified port
questions.explanation: `app.listen(3000, () => console.log('Server running'))` starts the server on port 3000.

questions.question: What does `res.json(data)` do?
options: Sends a JSON response with Content-Type: application/json header automatically set
questions.answer: Sends a JSON response with Content-Type: application/json header automatically set
questions.explanation: `res.json({ success: true })` serializes the object, sets the correct header, and ends the response.

questions.question: What does `res.status(code)` do?
options: Sets the HTTP status code for the response — chainable with other methods
questions.answer: Sets the HTTP status code for the response — chainable with other methods
questions.explanation: `res.status(404).json({ error: 'Not found' })` sets status and sends JSON in one chain.

questions.question: What is `res.send()` in Express?
options: Sends an HTTP response with auto-detected Content-Type based on the argument type
questions.answer: Sends an HTTP response with auto-detected Content-Type based on the argument type
questions.explanation: `res.send(string)` → text/html, `res.send(Buffer)` → application/octet-stream, `res.send(object)` → JSON.

questions.question: How do you define HTTP method routes in Express?
options: Using app.get(), app.post(), app.put(), app.delete(), app.patch() methods
questions.answer: Using app.get(), app.post(), app.put(), app.delete(), app.patch() methods
questions.explanation: Each HTTP method has a corresponding Express method. `app.get('/users', handler)` handles GET /users.

questions.question: What is `express.Router()` and why use it?
options: Creates a mini-application (router) for modular, mountable route handlers
questions.answer: Creates a mini-application (router) for modular, mountable route handlers
questions.explanation: `express.Router()` creates a router instance for organizing routes by feature (e.g., `usersRouter`, `productsRouter`).

questions.question: What is error-handling middleware in Express?
options: A middleware with exactly 4 parameters (err, req, res, next) — Express identifies it as error middleware by arity
questions.answer: A middleware with exactly 4 parameters (err, req, res, next) — Express identifies it as error middleware by arity
questions.explanation: Error handlers must have 4 parameters. They run when `next(err)` is called or an error is thrown in async code.

questions.question: How do you pass an error to Express error handlers?
options: Call next(error) — passing any truthy value to next() routes to error middleware
questions.answer: Call next(error) — passing any truthy value to next() routes to error middleware
questions.explanation: Calling `next(err)` skips all remaining regular middleware and routes, jumping to error-handling middleware.

questions.question: What is `cors` package in Express?
options: Middleware that adds Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers to allow cross-domain requests
questions.answer: Middleware that adds Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers to allow cross-domain requests
questions.explanation: `app.use(cors())` adds appropriate `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers to enable CORS for all origins.

questions.question: What is `express-rate-limit`?
options: Middleware that limits repeated requests from the same IP within a time window to prevent abuse
questions.answer: Middleware that limits repeated requests from the same IP within a time window to prevent abuse
questions.explanation: Rate limiting prevents brute-force attacks and API abuse by returning 429 Too Many Requests after a threshold.

questions.question: What does `helmet` middleware do in Express?
options: Sets various security-related HTTP response headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) to harden the app
questions.answer: Sets various security-related HTTP response headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) to harden the app
questions.explanation: `helmet()` is a collection of 14+ middleware that set security headers, protecting against common web vulnerabilities.

questions.question: What is `app.route()` in Express?
options: Chains multiple HTTP method handlers for a single path to reduce code repetition
questions.answer: Chains multiple HTTP method handlers for a single path to reduce code repetition
questions.explanation: `app.route('/users').get(getUsers).post(createUser).put(updateUser)` handles all methods for `/users` cleanly.

questions.question: What is `multer` in Express?
options: Middleware for handling multipart/form-data requests, primarily for file uploads
questions.answer: Middleware for handling multipart/form-data requests, primarily for file uploads
questions.explanation: `multer` parses `multipart/form-data` and provides uploaded files via `req.file` (single) or `req.files` (multiple).

questions.question: What is `express-validator`?
options: A library for validating and sanitizing request data (body, params, query) with chainable validators
questions.answer: A library for validating and sanitizing request data (body, params, query) with chainable validators
questions.explanation: `express-validator` uses `check()`, `body()`, `validationResult()` for comprehensive input validation.

questions.question: What is JWT-based authentication pattern in Express?
options: Stateless auth where the server signs a token on login; client sends it in Authorization header for protected routes
questions.answer: Stateless auth where the server signs a token on login; client sends it in Authorization header for protected routes
questions.explanation: JWT auth: server returns `jwt.sign(payload, secret)` on login. Client sends `Authorization: Bearer token` header. Middleware verifies it.

questions.question: What is `passport.js` used with Express?
options: Authentication middleware supporting 500+ strategies (local, JWT, OAuth, Google, GitHub)
questions.answer: Authentication middleware supporting 500+ strategies (local, JWT, OAuth, Google, GitHub)
questions.explanation: Passport.js abstracts authentication into strategies, integrating seamlessly with Express session or JWT flows.

questions.question: What is `express-session` package?
options: Session middleware that creates and manages user sessions with server-side storage
questions.answer: Session middleware that creates and manages user sessions with server-side storage
questions.explanation: `express-session` creates session objects stored server-side (memory, Redis, DB) with a session ID cookie.

questions.question: What does `cookie-parser` middleware do?
options: Parses the Cookie header and populates req.cookies with an object of cookie key-value pairs
questions.answer: Parses the Cookie header and populates req.cookies with an object of cookie key-value pairs
questions.explanation: `app.use(cookieParser())` makes `req.cookies` available. Use `req.signedCookies` for signed cookies.

questions.question: What does `res.redirect(url)` do?
options: Sends a redirect HTTP response to the client (default 302 Found) to a new URL
questions.answer: Sends a redirect HTTP response to the client (default 302 Found) to a new URL
questions.explanation: `res.redirect(301, '/new-url')` sends a permanent redirect. The browser follows it automatically.

questions.question: What is `app.all()` in Express?
options: Registers a route handler for ALL HTTP methods at a specified path
questions.answer: Registers a route handler for ALL HTTP methods at a specified path
questions.explanation: `app.all('/secret', handler)` responds to GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc. at `/secret`.

questions.question: What is `res.locals` in Express?
options: An object scoped to a single request-response cycle, accessible in middleware and templates
questions.answer: An object scoped to a single request-response cycle, accessible in middleware and templates
questions.explanation: `res.locals.user = currentUser` in middleware makes `user` available in subsequent middleware and view templates.

questions.question: What does `express.urlencoded()` middleware do?
options: Parses incoming requests with URL-encoded payloads (HTML form data) and populates req.body
questions.answer: Parses incoming requests with URL-encoded payloads (HTML form data) and populates req.body
questions.explanation: `express.urlencoded({ extended: true })` parses `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` form submissions.

questions.question: What is `req.headers` in Express?
options: An object containing all HTTP request headers as lowercase key-value pairs
questions.answer: An object containing all HTTP request headers as lowercase key-value pairs
questions.explanation: `req.headers['authorization']` or `req.get('Authorization')` reads the Authorization header (get() is case-insensitive).

questions.question: What is `res.set()` in Express?
options: Sets one or multiple HTTP response headers
questions.answer: Sets one or multiple HTTP response headers
questions.explanation: `res.set('Content-Type', 'text/html')` or `res.set({ 'X-Custom': 'value', 'Cache-Control': 'no-store' })` sets headers.

questions.question: What is a template engine in Express?
options: A library (EJS, Pug, Handlebars) that renders HTML templates with dynamic data on the server
questions.answer: A library (EJS, Pug, Handlebars) that renders HTML templates with dynamic data on the server
questions.explanation: Template engines compile templates with injected data into HTML strings, sent as the HTTP response via `res.render()`.

questions.question: What does `res.render('view', data)` do?
options: Renders a template view with the provided data object and sends the resulting HTML
questions.answer: Renders a template view with the provided data object and sends the resulting HTML
questions.explanation: `res.render('index', { title: 'Home', user })` compiles the `index` template with data and sends HTML.

questions.question: What is `morgan` used for in Express?
options: HTTP request logging middleware that logs method, URL, status, and response time
questions.answer: HTTP request logging middleware that logs method, URL, status, and response time
questions.explanation: Morgan (`app.use(morgan('dev'))`) logs HTTP requests in formats like 'tiny', 'dev', 'combined' for debugging.

questions.question: What does `res.download(filePath)` do?
options: Sends a file as a downloadable HTTP attachment, prompting the browser to download
questions.answer: Sends a file as a downloadable HTTP attachment, prompting the browser to download
questions.explanation: `res.download('/reports/report.pdf', 'monthly-report.pdf')` sends the file with Content-Disposition: attachment.

questions.question: What does `res.sendFile(path)` do?
options: Sends a file as the HTTP response with appropriate Content-Type header
questions.answer: Sends a file as the HTTP response with appropriate Content-Type header
questions.explanation: `res.sendFile(path.resolve('files/image.png'))` serves the file content — requires an absolute path.

questions.question: What is `req.ip` in Express?
options: The IP address of the requesting client
questions.answer: The IP address of the requesting client
questions.explanation: `req.ip` returns the client's IP address. With `trust proxy` enabled, it reads from X-Forwarded-For header.

questions.question: What is `trust proxy` setting in Express?
options: Enables Express to trust X-Forwarded-* headers from proxies/load balancers for correct IP/protocol detection
questions.answer: Enables Express to trust X-Forwarded-* headers from proxies/load balancers for correct IP/protocol detection
questions.explanation: `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` tells Express to trust one hop of proxy, enabling `req.ip` and `req.secure` behind a proxy.

questions.question: What is `app.param()` in Express?
options: Adds a callback that runs when a specified route parameter is present, for pre-processing
questions.answer: Adds a callback that runs when a specified route parameter is present, for pre-processing
questions.explanation: `app.param('userId', (req, res, next, id) => { req.user = findUser(id); next(); })` centralizes param processing.

questions.question: What does `res.type(type)` do?
options: Sets the Content-Type HTTP response header using MIME type or file extension shorthand
questions.answer: Sets the Content-Type HTTP response header using MIME type or file extension shorthand
questions.explanation: `res.type('json')` sets `Content-Type: application/json`. `res.type('text/html')` sets HTML.

questions.question: What is `res.cookie(name, value, options)` in Express?
options: Sets an HTTP cookie in the Set-Cookie response header with optional security options
questions.answer: Sets an HTTP cookie in the Set-Cookie response header with optional security options
questions.explanation: `res.cookie('token', value, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'strict' })` sets a secure cookie.

questions.question: What is async error handling in Express?
options: Wrapping async route handlers with try-catch and calling next(err), or using express-async-errors package
questions.answer: Wrapping async route handlers with try-catch and calling next(err), or using express-async-errors package
questions.explanation: Express doesn't catch async errors by default. Use `try { await op() } catch(e) { next(e) }` or `express-async-errors`.

questions.question: What is `x-powered-by` header and should you disable it?
options: Reveals 'Express' as the framework — should be disabled in production to reduce attack surface
questions.answer: Reveals 'Express' as the framework — should be disabled in production to reduce attack surface
questions.explanation: `app.disable('x-powered-by')` removes the header that advertises the framework, reducing information exposure.

questions.question: What is the difference between `app.get()` and `router.get()`?
options: app.get() registers on the app instance; router.get() is for modular Router instances
questions.answer: app.get() registers on the app instance; router.get() is for modular Router instances
questions.explanation: Use `router.get()` in feature-specific router files, then mount the router with `app.use('/api', router)`.

questions.question: What is `req.fresh` in Express?
options: True when the response is considered fresh based on Last-Modified and ETag cache headers
questions.answer: True when the response is considered fresh based on Last-Modified and ETag cache headers
questions.explanation: `req.fresh` allows conditional GET — if true, you can respond 304 Not Modified to save bandwidth.

questions.question: What is SSE (Server-Sent Events) in Express?
options: A technique for pushing real-time updates from server to client over a persistent HTTP connection
questions.answer: A technique for pushing real-time updates from server to client over a persistent HTTP connection
questions.explanation: SSE uses `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `res.write()` in a loop, and the browser's EventSource API for real-time updates.

questions.question: What is `compression` middleware in Express?
options: Middleware that gzip/deflates HTTP responses to reduce payload size and improve transfer speed
questions.answer: Middleware that gzip/deflates HTTP responses to reduce payload size and improve transfer speed
questions.explanation: `app.use(compression())` automatically compresses responses above a threshold, improving performance.

questions.question: What is `method-override` middleware?
options: Allows using HTTP verbs like PUT and DELETE from HTML forms that only support GET and POST
questions.answer: Allows using HTML forms that only support GET and POST to use PUT, DELETE via a query parameter or header
questions.explanation: `method-override` checks `X-HTTP-Method-Override` header or `_method` query param to override the HTTP method.

questions.question: What is `body-parser` and its relationship to Express?
options: Formerly a separate package; its core functionality (json, urlencoded) is now built into Express 4.16+
questions.answer: Formerly a separate package; its core functionality (json, urlencoded) is now built into Express 4.16+
questions.explanation: Since Express 4.16, use `express.json()` and `express.urlencoded()` instead of the separate `body-parser` package.

questions.question: What is `req.path` in Express?
options: The path portion of the request URL, excluding query string and domain
questions.answer: The path portion of the request URL, excluding query string and domain
questions.explanation: For `GET /users?page=2`, `req.path` is `/users` (without the query string).

questions.question: What is `res.end()` vs `res.send()` in Express?
options: res.end() is Node's raw method (no body processing); res.send() adds content-type, encoding, and ETag
questions.answer: res.end() is Node's raw method (no body processing); res.send() adds content-type, encoding, and ETag
questions.explanation: Prefer `res.send()` or `res.json()` in Express. `res.end()` is useful for streaming or when no body is needed.

questions.question: What is `app.locals` in Express?
options: Application-level variables accessible throughout the app lifetime and in all templates
questions.answer: Application-level variables accessible throughout the app lifetime and in all templates
questions.explanation: `app.locals.appName = 'MyApp'` makes `appName` available in all templates, unlike `res.locals` which is request-scoped.

questions.question: What is `req.method` in Express?
options: A string containing the HTTP method of the request: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.
questions.answer: A string containing the HTTP method of the request: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.
questions.explanation: `req.method` is always uppercase: 'GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE', 'PATCH', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS'.

questions.question: What is `req.get(headerName)` in Express?
options: Returns the specified HTTP request header value (case-insensitive)
questions.answer: Returns the specified HTTP request header value (case-insensitive)
questions.explanation: `req.get('Content-Type')` and `req.get('content-type')` both return the Content-Type header value.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `next('route')` in Express?
options: Goes to the next route file
Skips remaining handlers in the current route and passes to the next matching route
questions.answer: Skips remaining handlers in the current route and passes to the next matching route
questions.explanation: `next('route')` in a route handler skips subsequent handlers for the same route, moving to the next route definition.

questions.question: What is `res.append()` in Express?
options: Appends additional values to an existing response header or creates it if it doesn't exist
questions.answer: Appends additional values to an existing response header or creates it if it doesn't exist
questions.explanation: `res.append('Set-Cookie', 'token=abc')` adds a cookie header without overwriting existing Set-Cookie headers.

questions.question: What is `req.accepts()` in Express?
options: Checks if the client accepts the specified content types based on the Accept header
questions.answer: Checks if the client accepts the specified content types based on the Accept header
questions.explanation: `req.accepts(['json', 'html'])` returns the best match from the client's Accept header or false if none match.

questions.question: What is `res.format()` in Express?
options: Performs content negotiation — calls different response handlers based on the request's Accept header
questions.answer: Performs content negotiation — calls different response handlers based on the request's Accept header
questions.explanation: `res.format({ 'text/html': htmlHandler, 'application/json': jsonHandler })` responds in the client's preferred format.

questions.question: What is `req.hostname` in Express?
options: The hostname extracted from the Host HTTP header (e.g., 'example.com')
questions.answer: The hostname extracted from the Host HTTP header (e.g., 'example.com')
questions.explanation: `req.hostname` returns the hostname from the Host header. With `trust proxy`, it reads from X-Forwarded-Host.

questions.question: What is `req.protocol` in Express?
options: 'http' or 'https' — the protocol of the request
questions.answer: 'http' or 'https' — the protocol of the request
questions.explanation: `req.protocol` returns the request protocol. With `trust proxy`, it reads from X-Forwarded-Proto.

questions.question: What is `req.secure` in Express?
options: True if the request was made over HTTPS (shorthand for req.protocol === 'https')
questions.answer: True if the request was made over HTTPS (shorthand for req.protocol === 'https')
questions.explanation: `req.secure` is `true` for HTTPS requests, useful for enforcing HTTPS redirects.

questions.question: What is clustering in Express?js?
options: Using Node.js cluster module to spawn one process per CPU core, each running the Express app
questions.answer: Using Node.js cluster module to spawn one process per CPU core, each running the Express app
questions.explanation: Clustering maximizes CPU utilization. Each worker process runs an Express instance, with the OS balancing connections.

questions.question: What is `express-async-errors` package?
options: A monkey-patch that automatically catches async errors in Express route handlers and passes to next(err)
questions.answer: A monkey-patch that automatically catches async errors in Express route handlers and passes to next(err)
questions.explanation: `require('express-async-errors')` eliminates the need for try-catch in every async route — errors propagate to error middleware automatically.

questions.question: What is input sanitization in Express?
options: Removing/escaping dangerous characters from user input to prevent XSS and injection attacks
questions.answer: Removing/escaping dangerous characters from user input to prevent XSS and injection attacks
questions.explanation: Sanitization cleans input (trim, escape HTML, remove SQL characters) to prevent injection. Use `express-validator` or `DOMPurify`.

questions.question: What is the order of middleware execution in Express?
options: Top-to-bottom in the order they are registered with app.use() or route methods
questions.answer: Top-to-bottom in the order they are registered with app.use() or route methods
questions.explanation: Express executes middleware in registration order. Global middleware must be registered before routes to run on all requests.

questions.question: What is `req.originalUrl` vs `req.url`?
options: req.originalUrl is the full original URL; req.url is relative to the mount path in sub-routers
questions.answer: req.originalUrl is the full original URL; req.url is relative to the mount path in sub-routers
questions.explanation: When mounted at `/api`, inside the router `req.url` is `/users` but `req.originalUrl` is `/api/users`.

questions.question: What is response streaming in Express?
options: Sending large responses in chunks using res.write() followed by res.end()
questions.answer: Sending large responses in chunks using res.write() followed by res.end()
questions.explanation: For large files or real-time data, `res.write(chunk)` sends data incrementally without buffering the entire response.

questions.question: What is `res.vary(field)` in Express?
options: Adds a field to the Vary response header, informing caches which headers affect the response
questions.answer: Adds a field to the Vary response header, informing caches which headers affect the response
questions.explanation: `res.vary('Accept-Encoding')` tells caches to store separate versions based on Accept-Encoding.

questions.question: What is the `sub-app` pattern in Express?
options: Mounting a separate Express app as middleware inside another app for modular architecture
questions.answer: Mounting a separate Express app as middleware inside another app for modular architecture
questions.explanation: `mainApp.use('/admin', adminApp)` mounts a separate Express instance at `/admin` for independent configuration.

questions.question: What is `app.engine()` in Express?
options: Registers a template engine for a custom file extension or overrides the default engine
questions.answer: Registers a template engine for a custom file extension or overrides the default engine
questions.explanation: `app.engine('html', require('ejs').renderFile)` makes Express render `.html` files using EJS.

questions.question: What is `router.route()` in Express?
options: Chains multiple HTTP method handlers on a Router instance for a single path — same as app.route() but on Router
questions.answer: Chains multiple HTTP method handlers on a Router instance for a single path — same as app.route() but on Router
questions.explanation: `router.route('/users').get(list).post(create)` is the modular equivalent of `app.route()`.

questions.question: What is `express.raw()` middleware?
options: Parses incoming requests with raw binary (Buffer) payloads, before any processing
questions.answer: Parses incoming requests with raw binary (Buffer) payloads, before any processing
questions.explanation: `express.raw({ type: 'application/octet-stream' })` makes `req.body` a Buffer for binary uploads like webhooks with raw payloads.

questions.title: Java MCQ Quiz – 75 Multiple Choice Questions with Answers
questions.seo_description: Master Java with 75 MCQs covering OOP, collections, streams, concurrency, generics, JVM internals, design patterns, and Java 17/21 features. Essential for Java developer interviews.
questions.intro: Java is one of the world's most widely used programming languages, powering enterprise applications, Android development, and backend systems. These 75 MCQs cover Java fundamentals including OOP, collections framework, generics, streams API, concurrency, JVM internals, modern Java features (records, sealed classes, virtual threads), and design patterns.

questions.question: What is Java?
options: A platform-independent, object-oriented, strongly-typed programming language that compiles to bytecode
questions.answer: A platform-independent, object-oriented, strongly-typed programming language that compiles to bytecode
questions.explanation: Java compiles to bytecode that runs on any JVM, delivering 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' platform independence.

questions.question: What is the JVM?
options: Java Virtual Machine — the runtime that executes Java bytecode
questions.answer: Java Virtual Machine — the runtime that executes Java bytecode
questions.explanation: The JVM is an abstract machine that provides the runtime environment to execute Java bytecode, handling memory management and JIT compilation.

questions.question: What is the difference between JDK and JRE?
options: JDK includes development tools (compiler, debugger) + JRE; JRE is runtime-only
questions.answer: JDK includes development tools (compiler, debugger) + JRE; JRE is runtime-only
questions.explanation: JRE is needed to run Java programs. JDK is needed to develop and compile them. JDK includes JRE plus javac, javap, etc.

questions.question: What are the four pillars of OOP in Java?
questions.answer: Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, Abstraction
questions.explanation: These four principles form the foundation of object-oriented design in Java.

questions.question: What is the difference between method overriding and method overloading?
options: Overriding redefines a parent's method in a subclass (runtime); overloading defines multiple methods with the same name but different params (compile-time)
questions.answer: Overriding redefines a parent's method in a subclass (runtime); overloading defines multiple methods with the same name but different params (compile-time)
questions.explanation: Overriding is runtime polymorphism (same signature, different implementation). Overloading is compile-time polymorphism (same name, different params).

questions.question: What is the difference between `==` and `.equals()` in Java?
options: `==` compares object references; `.equals()` compares object content (logical equality)
questions.answer: `==` compares object references; `.equals()` compares object content (logical equality)
questions.explanation: For objects, `==` checks memory addresses. `.equals()` (when properly overridden) checks logical equality (content).

questions.question: What is an interface in Java?
options: A reference type defining a contract of abstract methods (and since Java 8, default/static methods)
questions.answer: A reference type defining a contract of abstract methods (and since Java 8, default/static methods)
questions.explanation: Interfaces define a contract. From Java 8, they can have `default` and `static` methods. From Java 9, `private` methods too.

questions.question: What is an abstract class in Java?
options: A class that can have abstract and concrete methods but cannot be instantiated directly
A class with only abstract methods
questions.answer: A class that can have abstract and concrete methods but cannot be instantiated directly
questions.explanation: Abstract classes can have state (fields), constructors, and both abstract and concrete methods — unlike interfaces.

questions.question: What is the Java Collections Framework?
options: A set of Java collections only
A unified architecture of interfaces (List, Set, Map, Queue) and implementations (ArrayList, HashMap) for data storage
questions.answer: A unified architecture of interfaces (List, Set, Map, Queue) and implementations (ArrayList, HashMap) for data storage
questions.explanation: The Collections Framework provides reusable data structures and algorithms, reducing programming effort.

questions.question: What is the difference between `ArrayList` and `LinkedList`?
options: ArrayList uses a dynamic array for O(1) random access; LinkedList uses doubly-linked nodes for O(1) head/tail insertions
questions.answer: ArrayList uses a dynamic array for O(1) random access; LinkedList uses doubly-linked nodes for O(1) head/tail insertions
questions.explanation: Choose ArrayList for frequent reads by index. Choose LinkedList for frequent insertions/deletions at the front/middle.

questions.question: What is `HashMap` in Java?
options: A hash table implementation of Map providing O(1) average-case get/put with no ordering guarantees
questions.answer: A hash table implementation of Map providing O(1) average-case get/put with no ordering guarantees
questions.explanation: HashMap uses hashing for fast lookups. It's not thread-safe and allows one null key. Not ordered.

questions.question: What is `ConcurrentHashMap`?
options: A thread-safe Map implementation using segment-level locking (Java 7) or CAS operations (Java 8+) for high concurrency
questions.answer: A thread-safe Map implementation using segment-level locking (Java 7) or CAS operations (Java 8+) for high concurrency
questions.explanation: ConcurrentHashMap allows concurrent reads and writes without locking the entire map, unlike `Collections.synchronizedMap()`.

questions.question: What are generics in Java?
options: Type parameters that enable writing type-safe, reusable code without explicit casting
questions.answer: Type parameters that enable writing type-safe, reusable code without explicit casting
questions.explanation: `List<String>` catches type errors at compile time. Without generics, you'd need casts and risk ClassCastException at runtime.

questions.question: What is the Java Streams API?
options: A functional-style API (Java 8+) for declarative processing of collections with operations like filter, map, reduce
questions.answer: A functional-style API (Java 8+) for declarative processing of collections with operations like filter, map, reduce
questions.explanation: Streams process data declaratively and can run sequentially or in parallel without mutating the source collection.

questions.question: What is `Optional<T>` in Java?
options: A container object that may or may not hold a non-null value, used to avoid NullPointerException
questions.answer: A container object that may or may not hold a non-null value, used to avoid NullPointerException
questions.explanation: `Optional.of(value)`, `Optional.empty()`, `optional.isPresent()`, `optional.orElse(default)` provide safe null handling.

questions.question: What is a lambda expression in Java?
options: A concise anonymous function implementing a functional interface, passed as an argument
questions.answer: A concise anonymous function implementing a functional interface, passed as an argument
questions.explanation: Lambda expressions `(a, b) -> a + b` implement a single-method interface concisely without anonymous class boilerplate.

questions.question: What is a functional interface?
options: An interface with exactly one abstract method — can be implemented by a lambda expression
questions.answer: An interface with exactly one abstract method — can be implemented by a lambda expression
questions.explanation: The `@FunctionalInterface` annotation enforces this. Examples: `Runnable`, `Comparator`, `Predicate`, `Function`.

questions.question: What are common built-in functional interfaces in Java?
options: Function<T,R>, Predicate<T>, Consumer<T>, Supplier<T> in java.util.function
questions.answer: Function<T,R>, Predicate<T>, Consumer<T>, Supplier<T> in java.util.function
questions.explanation: `Function` transforms T to R. `Predicate` tests a condition. `Consumer` consumes input. `Supplier` provides output.

questions.question: What does the `synchronized` keyword do?
options: Ensures only one thread can execute the synchronized block/method at a time, using an intrinsic lock
questions.answer: Ensures only one thread can execute the synchronized block/method at a time, using an intrinsic lock
questions.explanation: Synchronization prevents thread interference and memory consistency errors on shared mutable data.

questions.question: What is the `volatile` keyword in Java?
options: Ensures that reads and writes to a variable go directly to main memory, providing visibility across threads
questions.answer: Ensures that reads and writes to a variable go directly to main memory, providing visibility across threads
questions.explanation: `volatile` prevents threads from caching a variable locally. It guarantees visibility but not atomicity for compound operations.

questions.question: What is `ExecutorService` in Java?
options: A framework for managing and reusing thread pools, submitting tasks as Runnable or Callable
questions.answer: A framework for managing and reusing thread pools, submitting tasks as Runnable or Callable
questions.explanation: `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4)` creates a pool. `submit(task)` returns a `Future<T>` for the result.

questions.question: What is `CompletableFuture` in Java?
options: A Future with composable async operations (thenApply, thenCompose, allOf, anyOf) for non-blocking code
questions.answer: A Future with composable async operations (thenApply, thenCompose, allOf, anyOf) for non-blocking code
questions.explanation: `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> ...).thenApply(v -> ...).exceptionally(e -> ...)` chains async tasks elegantly.

questions.question: What is String immutability in Java?
options: Once created, a String's character sequence cannot change — any modification creates a new String object
questions.answer: Once created, a String's character sequence cannot change — any modification creates a new String object
questions.explanation: Immutability enables String pool caching, thread safety, and safe use as HashMap keys.

questions.question: What is the String pool in Java?
options: A cache of String literals in the heap, allowing strings with the same content to share the same object
questions.answer: A cache of String literals in the heap, allowing strings with the same content to share the same object
questions.explanation: String literals are interned automatically. `str.intern()` adds a String to the pool manually, enabling reference comparison.

questions.question: What is `StringBuilder` vs `StringBuffer`?
options: StringBuilder is not thread-safe but faster for single-threaded use; StringBuffer is thread-safe (synchronized)
questions.answer: StringBuilder is not thread-safe but faster for single-threaded use; StringBuffer is thread-safe (synchronized)
questions.explanation: Prefer `StringBuilder` for single-threaded string building. `StringBuffer` adds synchronization overhead — use only when needed.

questions.question: What is garbage collection in Java?
options: Automatic memory management that identifies and frees objects no longer reachable by any reference
questions.answer: Automatic memory management that identifies and frees objects no longer reachable by any reference
questions.explanation: The GC (G1GC, ZGC, Shenandoah) automatically reclaims heap memory, eliminating manual memory management.

questions.question: What is the difference between `final`, `finally`, and `finalize()`?
options: final: immutability keyword; finally: always-runs try block; finalize(): deprecated pre-GC cleanup method
questions.answer: final: immutability keyword; finally: always-runs try block; finalize(): deprecated pre-GC cleanup method
questions.explanation: `final` on a class/method/variable prevents extension/override/reassignment. `finalize()` was removed in Java 18.

questions.question: What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?
options: Checked exceptions must be declared with throws or caught; unchecked (RuntimeException subclasses) don't require handling
questions.answer: Checked exceptions must be declared with throws or caught; unchecked (RuntimeException subclasses) don't require handling
questions.explanation: Checked: IOException, SQLException. Unchecked: NullPointerException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Controversial design choice.

questions.question: What is autoboxing and unboxing in Java?
options: Automatic conversion between primitive types (int, double) and their wrapper classes (Integer, Double)
questions.answer: Automatic conversion between primitive types (int, double) and their wrapper classes (Integer, Double)
questions.explanation: Autoboxing: `Integer i = 5` (int→Integer). Unboxing: `int x = new Integer(5)` (Integer→int). Be careful with NullPointerException from unboxing null.

questions.question: What is Java `record` (Java 16)?
options: An immutable data carrier class with auto-generated constructor, getters, equals, hashCode, and toString
questions.answer: An immutable data carrier class with auto-generated constructor, getters, equals, hashCode, and toString
questions.explanation: `record Point(int x, int y) {}` automatically generates all boilerplate, replacing verbose data classes.

questions.question: What are sealed classes in Java (Java 17)?
options: Classes that restrict which specific classes may extend or implement them using permits clause
questions.answer: Classes that restrict which specific classes may extend or implement them using permits clause
questions.explanation: `sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Rectangle, Triangle` — only the listed types can implement it, enabling exhaustive pattern matching.

questions.question: What is pattern matching for `instanceof` (Java 16)?
options: Combines instanceof check with variable binding in one expression: `if (obj instanceof String s) { use s }`
questions.answer: Combines instanceof check with variable binding in one expression: `if (obj instanceof String s) { use s }`
questions.explanation: Pattern matching eliminates the explicit cast after an instanceof check, making the code more concise and safe.

questions.question: What is text block in Java (Java 15)?
options: A multi-line String literal using triple quotes that preserves formatting and avoids escape characters
questions.answer: A multi-line String literal using triple quotes that preserves formatting and avoids escape characters
questions.explanation: Text blocks: `"""SELECT * FROM users"""`  make multi-line SQL, JSON, HTML strings readable without `\n` and `+`.

questions.question: What is the switch expression (Java 14)?
options: An enhanced switch that returns a value and uses `case X ->` arrow syntax, eliminating fall-through
questions.answer: An enhanced switch that returns a value and uses `case X ->` arrow syntax, eliminating fall-through
questions.explanation: Switch expressions: `int result = switch(day) { case MON -> 1; case TUE -> 2; default -> 0; };` — concise, no fall-through.

questions.question: What is `var` keyword in Java (Java 10)?
options: Local variable type inference — the compiler infers the type from the initializer expression
questions.answer: Local variable type inference — the compiler infers the type from the initializer expression
questions.explanation: `var list = new ArrayList<String>()` infers `ArrayList<String>`. Only for local variables — not method params or fields.

questions.question: What is the `Stream.collect()` method?
options: A terminal operation that accumulates stream elements into a collection or summary value using a Collector
questions.answer: A terminal operation that accumulates stream elements into a collection or summary value using a Collector
questions.explanation: `stream.collect(Collectors.toList())`, `.groupingBy()`, `.joining()`, `.counting()` are common collectors.

questions.question: What is `flatMap()` in Java Streams?
options: Maps each element to a Stream, then flattens all resulting streams into a single stream
questions.answer: Maps each element to a Stream, then flattens all resulting streams into a single stream
questions.explanation: `listOfLists.stream().flatMap(Collection::stream)` merges nested collections into one flat stream.

questions.question: What is `Collectors.groupingBy()` in Java?
options: A downstream Collector that groups stream elements by a classifier function into Map<K, List<T>>
questions.answer: A downstream Collector that groups stream elements by a classifier function into Map<K, List<T>>
questions.explanation: `stream.collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Employee::getDept))` groups employees by department into a Map.

questions.question: What is `AtomicInteger` in Java?
options: An int value that supports atomic (compare-and-swap) operations without synchronization overhead
questions.answer: An int value that supports atomic (compare-and-swap) operations without synchronization overhead
questions.explanation: `AtomicInteger.getAndIncrement()` is atomic — no `synchronized` needed for thread-safe counters.

questions.question: What is `try-with-resources` in Java?
options: A try statement that automatically closes resources implementing AutoCloseable when the block exits
questions.answer: A try statement that automatically closes resources implementing AutoCloseable when the block exits
questions.explanation: `try (Connection conn = getConn(); Statement stmt = conn.createStatement()) { }` — both close automatically, even on exception.

questions.question: What is the `Comparable` interface?
options: An interface that defines natural ordering via `compareTo()` for use with sorting and TreeMap/TreeSet
questions.answer: An interface that defines natural ordering via `compareTo()` for use with sorting and TreeMap/TreeSet
questions.explanation: Classes implementing `Comparable<T>` define their natural order. `Collections.sort()` uses this automatically.

questions.question: What is the `Comparator` interface?
options: An interface for defining custom, external sort orders separate from the class, supporting multiple orderings
questions.answer: An interface for defining custom, external sort orders separate from the class, supporting multiple orderings
questions.explanation: `Comparator.comparing(Person::getName).thenComparing(Person::getAge)` chains sort criteria externally.

questions.question: What is the `Deque` interface in Java?
options: A double-ended queue interface supporting insertion and removal at both ends — implemented by ArrayDeque and LinkedList
questions.answer: A double-ended queue interface supporting insertion and removal at both ends — implemented by ArrayDeque and LinkedList
questions.explanation: `Deque` can be used as a stack (`push`/`pop`) or queue (`offer`/`poll`). `ArrayDeque` is preferred over Stack.

questions.question: What is `PriorityQueue` in Java?
options: An unbounded queue that always retrieves the smallest element (or as defined by Comparator) in O(log n)
questions.answer: An unbounded queue that always retrieves the smallest element (or as defined by Comparator) in O(log n)
questions.explanation: `PriorityQueue<Integer> pq = new PriorityQueue<>()` creates a min-heap. Use reverse order for max-heap.

questions.question: What is the `Enum` type in Java?
options: A special class type representing a fixed set of named constants with optional fields and methods
questions.answer: A special class type representing a fixed set of named constants with optional fields and methods
questions.explanation: Java enums are full classes: they can have constructors, fields, and methods. `enum Color { RED, GREEN, BLUE }`.

questions.question: What is the Singleton design pattern in Java?
options: A creational pattern ensuring a class has exactly one instance and provides a global access point
questions.answer: A creational pattern ensuring a class has exactly one instance and provides a global access point
questions.explanation: Implement with: private constructor, static instance field, `getInstance()` method. Use `enum Singleton` for thread safety.

questions.question: What is the Builder design pattern?
options: Constructs complex objects step-by-step using a fluent API, separating construction from representation
questions.answer: Constructs complex objects step-by-step using a fluent API, separating construction from representation
questions.explanation: Builder avoids telescoping constructors: `new Person.Builder().name('Alice').age(30).build()`.

questions.question: What is the Observer design pattern?
options: A behavioral pattern where subjects notify a list of observers when their state changes
questions.answer: A behavioral pattern where subjects notify a list of observers when their state changes
questions.explanation: Observer defines one-to-many dependency. Java has `Observable`/`Observer` (deprecated) — prefer event bus or listeners.

questions.question: What is Java reflection?
options: The ability to inspect and manipulate class structure (fields, methods, constructors) at runtime
questions.answer: The ability to inspect and manipulate class structure (fields, methods, constructors) at runtime
questions.explanation: `Class.forName('com.example.Foo').getDeclaredMethods()` examines classes dynamically. Used by frameworks like Spring.

questions.question: What is the `transient` keyword in Java?
options: Marks a field to be excluded from Java object serialization
questions.answer: Marks a field to be excluded from Java object serialization
questions.explanation: `transient String password` — the field won't be written to the byte stream when serializing the object.

questions.question: What are virtual threads in Java (Java 21)?
options: Lightweight JVM-managed threads from Project Loom enabling millions of concurrent operations without OS thread overhead
questions.answer: Lightweight JVM-managed threads from Project Loom enabling millions of concurrent operations without OS thread overhead
questions.explanation: Virtual threads `Thread.ofVirtual().start(task)` are scheduled by the JVM, enabling one thread per request models at scale.

questions.question: What is structured concurrency (Java 21)?
options: A concurrency API (`StructuredTaskScope`) treating a group of related tasks as a unit with automatic lifecycle management
questions.answer: A concurrency API (`StructuredTaskScope`) treating a group of related tasks as a unit with automatic lifecycle management
questions.explanation: `StructuredTaskScope.ShutdownOnFailure` cancels all sub-tasks if any fails, preventing partial failures.

questions.question: What is the `HashMap` vs `TreeMap` vs `LinkedHashMap`?
options: HashMap: O(1) unordered; TreeMap: O(log n) sorted by key; LinkedHashMap: O(1) insertion-ordered
questions.answer: HashMap: O(1) unordered; TreeMap: O(log n) sorted by key; LinkedHashMap: O(1) insertion-ordered
questions.explanation: Choose based on need: HashMap (performance), TreeMap (sorted order), LinkedHashMap (insertion/access order).

questions.question: What is `HashSet` vs `TreeSet` vs `LinkedHashSet`?
options: HashSet: O(1) no order; TreeSet: O(log n) sorted; LinkedHashSet: O(1) insertion-ordered, all unique
questions.answer: HashSet: O(1) no order; TreeSet: O(log n) sorted; LinkedHashSet: O(1) insertion-ordered, all unique
questions.explanation: All three store unique elements. Choose based on ordering requirements and performance needs.

questions.question: What is `default` method in interfaces (Java 8)?
options: A concrete method in an interface with a default implementation for backward compatibility
questions.answer: A concrete method in an interface with a default implementation for backward compatibility
questions.explanation: Default methods allow adding new functionality to interfaces without breaking existing implementing classes.

questions.question: What is method reference `::` in Java?
options: A shorthand for lambda expressions that call an existing method: `list.forEach(System.out::println)`
questions.answer: A shorthand for lambda expressions that call an existing method: `list.forEach(System.out::println)`
questions.explanation: Types: `Class::staticMethod`, `instance::method`, `Class::instanceMethod`, `Class::new` (constructor reference).

questions.question: What is `WeakReference` in Java?
options: A reference that doesn't prevent the referenced object from being garbage collected
questions.answer: A reference that doesn't prevent the referenced object from being garbage collected
questions.explanation: `WeakReference<T>` allows GC to collect the object when only weak references point to it. Used in caches like WeakHashMap.

questions.question: What is `StampedLock` in Java?
options: A read-write lock with an optimistic read mode that avoids full lock acquisition for read-heavy workloads
questions.answer: A read-write lock with an optimistic read mode that avoids full lock acquisition for read-heavy workloads
questions.explanation: `StampedLock` provides 3 modes: write lock, read lock, and optimistic read (no blocking) — best for read-heavy use cases.

questions.question: What is `Stream.parallel()` in Java?
options: Converts a sequential stream to a parallel stream that processes elements concurrently using ForkJoinPool
questions.answer: Converts a sequential stream to a parallel stream that processes elements concurrently using ForkJoinPool
questions.explanation: `.parallel()` splits the stream into chunks processed by ForkJoinPool. Useful for CPU-bound operations on large datasets.

questions.question: What is the `instanceof` pattern matching in switch (Java 21)?
options: Switch expressions that match on type patterns: `case String s -> s.length()`
questions.answer: Switch expressions that match on type patterns: `case String s -> s.length()`
questions.explanation: Pattern matching in switch enables exhaustive, type-safe handling: `switch(shape) { case Circle c -> c.area(); case Rect r -> r.area(); }`.

questions.question: What is `List.of()`, `Set.of()`, `Map.of()` in Java?
options: Static factory methods creating immutable collections (Java 9+) that throw UnsupportedOperationException on modification
questions.answer: Static factory methods creating immutable collections (Java 9+) that throw UnsupportedOperationException on modification
questions.explanation: `List.of(1, 2, 3)` creates a truly immutable list — no set(), add(), or remove() allowed.

questions.question: What is the `Flow` API in Java (Java 9)?
options: Publisher/Subscriber/Processor/Subscription interfaces for reactive streams — interoperable with RxJava and Reactor
questions.answer: Publisher/Subscriber/Processor/Subscription interfaces for reactive streams — interoperable with RxJava and Reactor
questions.explanation: Java `Flow` API is the standard reactive streams specification adapted for the JDK, enabling backpressure-aware async processing.

questions.question: What is `instanceof` without pattern matching vs with?
options: Without: `if (obj instanceof String) { String s = (String) obj; }` — explicit cast; With: `if (obj instanceof String s)` — automatic binding
questions.answer: Without: `if (obj instanceof String) { String s = (String) obj; }` — explicit cast; With: `if (obj instanceof String s)` — automatic binding
questions.explanation: Pattern matching (Java 16) eliminates the redundant cast, making type narrowing more concise and safe.

questions.question: What is `sealed interface` with `permits`?
options: An interface that explicitly lists which types can implement it, enabling exhaustive pattern matching in switch
questions.answer: An interface that explicitly lists which types can implement it, enabling exhaustive pattern matching in switch

questions.question: What is the `@FunctionalInterface` annotation?
options: Documents and enforces at compile time that an interface has exactly one abstract method
